table.reasoning: Both adapters trivially forward to a static parser API solely to satisfy a protocol for DI. Same algorithm — wrap a static type behind an instance protocol — repeated for two different parsers. A generic `StaticParserAdapter<T>` or a single shared pattern (e.g., closure-based protocol implementation) would remove the duplication.

findings.title: Static-API adapter pattern duplicated across files
findings.issue: LogParserAdapter (LogViewerView.swift:56) and DefaultSubagentParser (SubagentDetailView.swift:72) both exist solely to forward instance-protocol method calls to a static type's static methods. The wrapping pattern is identical in structure.
findings.impact: Each new parser dependency forces a new boilerplate adapter type. A reusable adapter abstraction or closure-based protocol injection would centralize the pattern.

table.responsibility_fit: Both render a list of {status, content} items with status-driven SF symbol icon, strikethrough on completed, and identical typography. todoChecklist works on TodoWriteToolData.TodoItem; taskPanelView's inner ForEach (lines 1246-1257) does the same thing for TaskListItem.
interface_differences: Item types differ (TodoItem vs TaskListItem) but both expose `content: String` and `status: String`
taskPanelView adds an extra 'deleted' status case

table.reasoning: Both methods are status-string → SF symbol name switches with identical control flow and overlapping cases ('completed' → checkmark.circle.fill, 'in_progress' → circle.dotted.circle, default → circle). taskIcon adds a 'deleted' case. The mapping is the same domain concept (task/todo status presentation).

Both methods are status-string → Color switches with identical control flow and overlapping cases ('completed' → green, 'in_progress' → orange, default → secondary). taskColor adds 'deleted' → red. Same mapping concern duplicated.

Both follow the same algorithm: split content into lines, branch on a line-count threshold to fall back to ToolResultView, otherwise render filePath header + ForEach over lines as monospaced/colored/padded/background-tinted rows wrapped in AnyView. editDiffView produces two stripes (- red, + green); writeDiffView produces one stripe (+ green). The per-line row rendering is identical save for the prefix character, color, and tint.

table.reuse_potential: Both `todoIcon`/`todoColor` and `taskIcon`/`taskColor` (and the SubagentDetailView could need it too) implement the same status-presentation knowledge inline. Extracting a single TaskStatusStyle abstraction (e.g., `enum TaskStatus { … } { var icon: String; var color: Color }`) would centralize the mapping and remove four parallel switches.

table.pattern: Line-by-line diff stripe row (monospaced text + leading prefix + tinted foreground/background + small padding)
table.reuse_potential: editDiffView and writeDiffView both render this row inline. A reusable `DiffLineRow(prefix:, line:, tint:)` view would let any future tool detail render diff stripes without copying the styling.

table.pattern: Permission button row sending raw escape sequences via bridge (Allow/Always/Deny / Approve/Reject)
table.reuse_potential: permissionPrompt (966) and planApprovalPrompt (1095) both compose an HStack of borderedProminent tinted buttons that call `bridge?.sendRaw(...)` with control codes. A reusable `PromptButtonRow(buttons: [PromptButton])` component would absorb both prompt variants and any future prompt type.

findings.title: todoChecklist and taskPanelView render the same checklist independently
findings.issue: todoChecklist (lines 911-928) and the per-row block inside taskPanelView (lines 1246-1259) render the same UI: status-icon + content text with strikethrough on completed. Item types differ but both expose `content` and `status`. The first implementation could be reused for the second via a small protocol or an explicit row view.
findings.impact: Visual drift — taskPanelView already diverges by adding a 'deleted' status. Future status changes must be repeated in two places.

findings.title: Status→icon and status→color switches duplicated for todos and tasks
findings.issue: todoIcon/taskIcon (930, 1265) and todoColor/taskColor (938, 1274) are four parallel switches over the same status-string vocabulary. Three of four cases are identical pairwise; only 'deleted' is unique to task*.
findings.impact: Any change to task status presentation (new status, color tweak) requires synchronized edits in four locations and risks divergence.

findings.title: editDiffView and writeDiffView duplicate diff row rendering
findings.issue: Both methods follow the identical algorithm: line-count threshold → fall back to ToolResultView; otherwise emit file path header + ForEach over lines styled as monospaced colored rows with tinted background, wrapped in AnyView. Only the prefix/colour and number of stripes differ.
findings.impact: Styling tweaks (font size, row padding, threshold) must be applied to both methods; future diff-style renderers will likely copy a third time.

findings.title: Missing abstraction: task/todo status presentation
findings.issue: Status→(icon, color) is a domain-agnostic mapping repeated four times inline (`todoIcon`, `todoColor`, `taskIcon`, `taskColor`). No standalone type captures this knowledge even though both LogViewerView and a hypothetical task panel elsewhere need the same behaviour.
findings.impact: The view holds presentation logic that other modules cannot share; any consumer of task status outside LogViewerView would have to re-implement the same switches.

findings.title: Missing abstraction: diff stripe line row
findings.issue: The per-line monospaced + prefix + tinted-foreground + tinted-background row used in both editDiffView and writeDiffView is a generic UI pattern (a coloured-stripe diff line) but is implemented inline both times.
findings.impact: Other future tool renderers (patch tool, replace_all preview, etc.) will likely re-implement the same row instead of reusing a `DiffLineRow` component.

findings.title: Missing abstraction: prompt button row
findings.issue: permissionPrompt (966) and planApprovalPrompt (1095) both compose an HStack of `.borderedProminent` tinted buttons that send raw escape sequences via `bridge?.sendRaw(...)`. The 'a row of styled action buttons that fire bridge writes' pattern is generic and not specific to either prompt's domain, but is duplicated inline.
findings.impact: Each new prompt type forces another bespoke HStack of buttons with copy-pasted padding/tint/controlSize code; styling is at risk of drifting.
